movesets.name: Assault Vest
movesets.description:
With an excellent Attack stat, STAB-boosted First Impression, and the momentum-generating U-turn complemented by Close Combat, Slither Wing establishes itself as an excellent choice on sun teams as a pivot and revenge killer. All of this while being a solid special tank with Assault Vest, allowing it to tank hits from faster special attackers such as Darkrai, offensive Gholdengo, and Glimmora more comfortably so that teammates can be pivoted in safely; the item also helps Slither Wing survive even OHKOs from moves such as Iron Moth’s sun-boosted Fiery Dance, opposing Walking Wake’s sun-boosted Draco Meteor, and Moonblast from Iron Valiant and Enamorus. With First Impression, Slither Wing can OHKO Darkrai, Ogerpon-W, and Weavile as well as pick off other chipped threats like Kyurem and Walking Wake. In sun, Close Combat lets Slither Wing 2HKO Great Tusk and Raging Bolt while also OHKOing Kyurem and Garganacl. U-turn allows it to generate momentum from predicted switches against foes that it threatens, such as Ting-Lu, forcing significant chip damage in the process, particularly against switchins like Galarian Weezing and Landorus-T. Earthquake is a safe option that hits Ground-weak Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking, Gholdengo without Air Balloon, and Iron Treads, without any drawbacks; however, it fails to threaten Corviknight and Air Balloon Gholdengo and loses out on various damage rolls, such as an OHKO on Iron Treads. Flare Blitz in sun enables OHKOs on Corviknight and Gholdengo at the cost of recoil damage that adds up over time, hurting Slither Wing's longevity as a pivot. Temper Flare is therefore a similar coverage option with the lack of drawback, and works well with its Close Combat after failing to hit incoming Ghost-types, particularly Gholdengo. Tera Steel allows Slither Wing to resist various Fairy- and Psychic-type moves that normally threaten it, such as Moonblast from Iron Valiant and Enamorus and Psyshock from Iron Crown. Tera Steel also reduces Stealth Rock damage, enhancing Slither Wing's ability to pivot further. Tera Fire is also a similar option against the Fairy-types, but also boosts its Fire coverage and prevents it from getting burned by foes like Moltres and Cinderace at the cost of being weak to Stealth Rock.

Slither Wing is almost exclusively found on sun teams that appreciate its ability to pivot, revenge kill foes that have been chipped, and threaten difficult matchups such as Garganacl and Galarian Slowking. Furthermore, Slither Wing appreciates Pokemon that benefit from sun and can capitalize on the momentum it generates while covering foes Slither Wing cannot threaten, such as Dragonite and Moltres. Torkoal provides Stealth Rock and entry hazard removal, so Slither Wing can pivot more consistently. Alternatively, Ninetales is a faster partner that offers excellent utility in Encore and Healing Wish and appreciates the slower pivoting Slither Wing provides to give it safe entry. Walking Wake loves the pivoting Slither Wing provides and appreciates its ability to take care of Walking Wake’s checks, such as Ogerpon-W and Blissey, via First Impression. In turn, Walking Wake's sheer power obliterates Gliscor, Moltres, and Landorus-T, which Slither Wing would otherwise struggle to dent. Like Torkoal, Great Tusk spins away entry hazards that threaten Slither Wing and provides a solid check to many Dragonite sets after Slither Wing breaks Multiscale with U-turn. On a similar vein, Hatterene denies most hazards, except Spikes from Hisuian Samurott, which is a foe that Slither Wing threatens. Raging Bolt is a good teammate as either a secondary pivot or setup sweeper. Raging Bolt complements Slither Wing by threatening Moltres, which could cripple it with a burn.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
Packing solid bulk and a surprisingly adept defensive typing that resists STAB moves from common offensive Pokemon such as Kingambit, Zamazenta, Great Tusk, Rillaboom, Hisuian Samurott, and Darkrai, Slither Wing serves as a specific but effective defensive pivot thanks to its ability to check many common threats in one teamslot. First Impression can revenge kill many important targets such as Ogerpon-W, Darkrai, and Weavile. U-Turn allows Slither Wing to maintain momentum while forcing out Pokemon that it can switch in on, such as Darkrai, Ogerpon-W, Rillaboom, and Hisuian Samurott. Morning Sun allows Slither Wing to stay healthy throughout a match, allowing it to check the previously mentioned Pokemon long-term. Lastly, Will-O-Wisp allow Slither Wing to cripple Pokemon it can't directly threaten, such as Great Tusk, Dragonite, Zamazenta, and Kingambit. 8 Speed EVs allow Slither Wing to outspeed Adamant Kingambit, while the 28 Attack EVs guarantees the OHKO on Darkrai with First Impression. Tera Steel is the Tera type of choice, allowing Slither Wing to check important threats it otherwise couldn't such as Latios. Tera Dragon is another solid option, giving a strong neutral defensive type that gives resistances to Ogerpon-W's STAB combination while granting a Fire resistance from foes like Cinderace.

Defensive Slither Wing functions best on bulky offense teams, using its good bulk, recovery, and U-turn to provide free switch-ins to its frailer teammates like Darkrai, Iron Valiant, Dragapult and Ogerpon-W. Slither Wing struggles against Moltres and Zapdos, the former punishes U-turn with Flame Body and absorbs Will-O-Wisp, and the latter does the same with Static and Stun Spore. Hard-hitting wallbreakers that can punish these two Pokemon switching in to either set up or wallbreak like Ogerpon-W, Ogerpon-C, Kyurem, and Raging Bolt make for good partners. Gholdengo is also another common roadblock for Slither Wing thanks to its typing, which lets it shrug off Slither Wing’s STAB combination, and Good As Gold, which makes it immune to all status moves, so strong Dark-types that can punish a Gholdengo switch like Darkrai, Hisuian Samurott, and Weavile are also effective partners. Slither Wing forms strong defensive cores with Pokemon like Moltres and Galarian Slowking that can take on offensive threats it cannot handle such as Iron Valiant, Kyurem, Gholdengo, and Primarina. Slither Wing, in return, provides a solid switch-in to the Dark-Types like Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, Lokix, and Weavile that force out Galarian Slowking as well as being a strong soft check to Ogerpon-W, which greatly threatens these defensive cores. Entry hazard setters such as Ting-Lu, Gliscor, and Landorus-T also make for good partners, as their hazards punish switches forced by First Impression.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Bug

Flare Blitz can be run to threaten Amoonguss, Scizor, and Forretress, while Wild Charge takes care of Pelipper and Gyarados. However, stacking Life Orb recoil with recoil from the aforementioned moves is not appreciated.

movesets.name: All-out Attacker (Bug)
movesets.description:
All-out attacker Slither Wing is a great option on Bug teams due to its part-Fighting typing and its access to First Impression and Close Combat, which let it deal with troublesome threats like Bisharp, Hisuian Goodra, and Iron Boulder. Close Combat is Slither Wing's strongest STAB move, which takes out Normal-, Rock-, Steel-, and Ice-types like Blissey, Garganacl, Hisuian Goodra, and Mamoswine. U-turn not only damages foes, but it also allows Slither Wing to pivot out into one of its teammates like Frosmoth. Morning Sun can be run over U-turn to increase Slither Wing's longevity throughout the battle, notably in the Steel matchup; however, doing so means Slither Wing lacks the key pivoting it gets from U-turn. First Impression provides priority for Slither Wing to deal with fast threats like Iron Boulder, Latios, and Darkrai. Earthquake allows Slither Wing to deal with Gholdengo while also threatening pesky Poison-types like Clodsire and 2HKOing Toxapex. Life Orb is the go-to item for Slither Wing so it can hit as hard as possible, notably giving it a chance to OHKO Ursaluna-B. Heavy-Duty Boots can be run over Life Orb to let Slither Wing ignore entry hazards and stay healthy. However, losing the additional power Life Orb provides is not appreciated. Adamant is its preferred nature, maximizing Slither Wing's damage to let it 2HKO Skarmory and specially defensive Corviknight with Life Orb-boosted Close Combat.

Choice Scarf Kleavor is a great teammate for Slither Wing, dealing with Flying- and Fire-types like Dragonite, Moltres, and Ogerpon-H with Stone Axe, which also sets Stealth Rock, weakening foes that Slither Wing can pick off with First Impression. Swords Dance Scizor at +2 can deal with troublesome Fairy- and Rock-types like Flutter Mane, Enamorus, and Choice Scarf Hisuian Arcanine. Slither Wing taking out Steel-types like Klefki and Bisharp means that Scizor has an easier time sweeping with Bullet Punch. Volcarona and Frosmoth are fierce setup sweepers that make for great partners; Volcarona at +1 deals with Galarian Weezing, Iron Valiant, and Great Tusk with Psychic and Giga Drain, while Frosmoth at +1 deals with Dragonite, Gliscor, and the Landorus formes with Ice Beam. Ribombee, Galvantula, and Araquanid all provide Sticky Web support, which allows Slither Wing to outspeed and eliminate threats like Ogerpon-H, Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine, and Choice Specs Iron Moth. Each Sticky Web setter also provides additional support for Slither Wing: Ribombee is the fastest of the setters and also threatens Dragon-, Dark-, and Fighting-types like Dragonite, Sableye, Iron Valiant, and Great Tusk, Galvantula eases the Flying and Water matchups thanks to its part-Electric typing and the combination of Thunder and Energy Ball, and Araquanid provides bulk while soaking up Fire-type attacks like Overheat from Ninetales under sun thanks to Water Bubble. Forretress removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin and provides slow pivoting for Slither Wing with Volt Switch to ensure safe entry.

This new Paradox Pokemon is likely to be relevant in Battle Stadium Singles Series 2. While we wait for the metagame to settle, here are some sample sets that may be viable. For more information on Series 2, check out the resource thread.

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description: Slither Wing's massive Attack stat alongside its powerful STAB moves makes it a strong wallbreaker, pivot, and revenge killer, able to threaten common physical walls like Corviknight, Deoxys-D, and Mandibuzz. First Impression lets Slither Wing pick off faster offensive threats like Chien-Pao, Latios, and Roaring Moon. Flare Blitz threatens Fluffy users like Corviknight, Zapdos, and Great Tusk as well as non-Well-Baked Body Gholdengo, while Earthquake threatens Ceruledge, Pecharunt, and non-Earth Eater Gholdengo. Tinted Lens helps Slither Wing revenge kill offensive threats like Dragonite, Zapdos, and Volcarona and boosts the power of U-turn against foes like Great Tusk, while Sword of Ruin lets Slither Wing OHKO Deoxys-D after entry hazard chip damage with U-turn, OHKO Fluffy Corviknight with Flare Blitz, OHKO Gholdengo with Earthquake, and 2HKO Defensive Great Tusk with Close Combat. While more niche, Scrappy lets it OHKO Gholdengo with Close Combat while still 2HKOing Intimidate Corviknight. Fast cleaners like Chien-Pao, Meowscarada, and Iron Boulder appreciate Slither Wing's ability to pressure their walls like Corviknight and Gholdengo, letting them sweep late-game once those walls have been chipped down or removed. Slither Wing's middling speed and only decent bulk leaves it vulnerable to offensive threats that do not fear First Impression like Ceruledge, Dragonite, and Azelf, making checks to them like Great Tusk, Corviknight, and Heatran, respectively, valuable teammates. Slither Wing is also prone to getting worn down by entry hazards, so hazard removers like Mandibuzz and the aforementioned Great Tusk and Corviknight are greatly appreciated.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 7-8 points

Overview: Slither Wing is a powerful physical attacker with access to many valuable moves, such as STAB U-turn and First Impression to effectively pivot and revenge kill, other strong STAB and coverage options, and utility options like Morning Sun and Will-O-Wisp. With Bulk Up and Flame Charge in its arsenal, Slither Wing can also be a fearsome setup sweeper. However, its incredibly average Speed gets it revenge killed by many Pokemon, especially those that resist its STAB combination. It also faces stiff competition from higher- or similarly-priced Fighting-types and is not helped by its mediocre bulk and weaknesses to common offensive types in Fairy, Flying, and Fire.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Wallbreaker: Slither Wing can equip damage-boosting items like Choice Band to dish out a lot of damage with powerful moves like Close Combat and Flare Blitz. This set generally runs U-turn to weaken checks and generate momentum and First Impression to revenge kill faster threats. Slither Wing can also equip a Choice Scarf to outspeed naturally faster Pokemon while still dealing a lot of damage, thanks to its high Attack stat.

Setup Sweeper: Slither Wing has access to both Bulk Up and Flame Charge and can utilize these to sweep unprepared teams. This set generally equips Booster Energy to gain a one-time boost to Attack to make it easier to sweep. Slither Wing can also run Morning Sun or Leech Life to keep itself healthy.

Utility: Slither Wing has useful resistances to Fighting, Dark, and Ground. Coupled with serviceable bulk when invested and access to reliable recovery, it can be used as a defensive switch-in to foes with the aforementioned typings. It also provides pivoting support as well as the ability to cripple opposing Pokemon with Will-O-Wisp or Stun Spore.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Close Combat, U-turn, Leech Life, First Impression, Low Kick, Brick Break

Setup Moves: Bulk Up, Flame Charge, Trailblaze

Utility Moves: Morning Sun, Will-O-Wisp, Stun Spore, Substitute

Coverage: Flare Blitz, Wild Charge, Earthquake, High Horsepower, Acrobatics, Zen Headbutt

Niche Moves

Whirlwind: Whirlwind is run in niche scenarios to phaze setup sweepers that Slither Wing can reliably take a hit from.

Lunge / Skitter Smack: Lunge or Skitter Smack can be run on defensive sets to weaken incoming checks or slow down setup sweepers.

Sunny Day: Slither Wing can run Sunny Day to activate Protosynthesis and boost Flare Blitz.

Common Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: As Slither Wing is vulnerable to every form of entry hazard, immunity to them is highly valuable, especially on sets focused on providing pivot support.

Choice Band: Choice Band is preferred over other damage-boosting items for maximum wallbreaking potential on teams that don't want to commit to the one-time use of Booster Energy to dish out a plethora of damage.

Booster Energy: Booster Energy gives Slither Wing a one-time boost to its Attack stat to start dealing massive damage to the opposing team. This enables Slither Wing to switch up moves and make use of its decent coverage moves. This is generally seen on setup sets, as it enables running a coverage or utility move over Bulk Up.

Niche Items

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Slither Wing to revenge kill faster Pokemon and become a fast pivot while dealing large amounts of damage with U-turn.

Rocky Helmet: Slither Wing's typing does well defensively against Bug-, Dark-, and Fighting-type attacks. Thus, Rocky Helmet can be used to switch in and punish Pokemon that run resisted moves like Knock Off, U-turn, and Close Combat.

Leftovers: Leftovers provides consistent recovery to bulkier utility sets, helping Slither Wing remain healthier to deal with opposing Pokemon.

Resistance Berries: Slither Wing has several common weaknesses, so it sometimes uses a resistance Berry to survive an attack that targets it for super effective damage, using the opportunity to deal damage or revenge kill opposing Pokemon.

Tera

While Slither Wing is a solid candidate for a Tera Captain, it should not be drafted for that purpose, as it is outclassed by several higher-tiered Tera Captains, and the opportunity cost is often not worth it. Further, it is a potent wallbreaker without needing the boost of Tera. It also provides useful resistances to a draft that would be lost with Tera. However, if chosen to be a Tera Captain, Slither Wing makes excellent use of STAB Tera types to further boost Close Combat, U-turn, and First Impression. It can also use Tera Fire or Tera Electric to boost its coverage options. On the defensive side, it can utilize Tera Steel to deal with Fairy-types or Tera Water to deal with Fire-types.

Draft Strategy

Slither Wing provides teams with an excellent wallbreaking option that is further able to support the team with its pivoting, priority, and useful resistances. While it can be a potent setup sweeper, setting up with it should not be a team's primary win condition. It also faces stiff competition from several Fighting-types, so it should only be drafted if it synergizes well with the rest of the team.

Faster Offensive Pokemon: As Slither Wing should not be the primary offensive option on a team, it works well with faster offensive teammates like Latios, Greninja, and Enamorus, supporting them with STAB U-turn pivoting as well as offering a reliable revenge killing option.

Flying-resistant Pokemon: Slither Wing is extremely vulnerable to Flying, often forcing foes to run Flying-type coverage. Pokemon like Rotom-W and Zapdos make great teammates, as they can switch in on Flying-types and form a solid VoltTurn core with Slither Wing.

Entry Hazard Support: Similar to other wallbreakers, Slither Wing appreciates teammates that can set entry hazards like Hisuian Samurott and Landorus-T to get vital chip damage on the opposing team. Additionally, as it is vulnerable to all forms of entry hazards, it appreciates strong hazard removal from teammates like Iron Treads and Glimmora to enable it to not rely on Heavy-Duty Boots and switch in more easily.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Flying-type Pokemon: Bulky Flying-type Pokemon like Gliscor, Landorus-T, and Zapdos resist Slither Wing's STAB combination, making them good switch-ins to Slither Wing. Zapdos and Moltres are especially annoying for their ability to cripple Slither Wing with Static and Flame Body, respectively.

Bulky Fairy-type Pokemon: Bulky Fairy-type Pokemon like Clefable and Azumarill resist Slither Wing's STAB moves and threaten a KO back.

Bulky Ghost-type Pokemon: Bulky Ghost-type Pokemon like Pecharunt and Annihilape are immune to Fighting and resist Bug, making them excellent defensive responses to Slither Wing.

Faster Pokemon: Slither Wing has subpar Speed and weaknesses to several common types, making it vulnerable to being revenge killed by faster Pokemon.
